extracted.intended_audience: legislators, statesmen, and informed citizens concerned with constitutional design (late-18th-century context)
extracted.subtask_description: A prescriptive critique of the French revolutionary Constitution offering principles and warnings for drafting durable republican constitutions: representation, local government, fiscal foundations, executive structure, and social/political habits. Focuses on what makes a constitution coherent, stable, and attentive to human nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to moral and political conditions of men
rubrics_metrics.description: Not one reference whatsoever is to be found to anything moral or anything politic,--nothing that relates to the concerns, the actions, the passions, the interests of men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislators must study human nature, habits, passions, and the effects of civil life (birth, education, profession, residence, property) when forming constitutions; purely metaphysical or mathematical schemes that ignore moral/political realities produce incoherent government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reconciling contradictory abstract principles
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not see a variety of objects reconciled in one consistent whole, but several contradictory principles reluctantly and irreconcilably brought and held together...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not base fundamental government arrangements on metaphysical/arithmetical abstractions or rigid geometric schemes; such approaches force incompatible principles together and undermine coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve substantive connections between central and local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not enter into the internal government of the departments... These local governments are, in the original plan, to be as nearly as possible composed in the same manner and on the same principles with the elective assemblies. They are each of them bodies perfectly compact and rounded in themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A constitution must provide constitutional means of coherence, connection, or subordination between local subdivisions and the central authority; leaving local units effectively independent risks severing the nation into disconnected republics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure representation is for the whole, not merely for parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Each deputy to the Assembly would be the representative of France, and of all its descriptions... The representative is a trustee for the whole, and not for the parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design representation so deputies act as trustees of the entire polity rather than ambassadors of fractional or sectional interests; a standing, fundamental government should be the point of reference uniting districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a clear and accountable link between electors and representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: To answer its real purposes, you must first possess the means of knowing the fitness of your man; and then you must retain some hold upon him by personal obligation or dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elections should enable electors to evaluate candidates' fitness and to hold them to account; excessive indirect or multi-stage electoral procedures that distance representatives from primary electors destroy effective accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multi-stage electoral gradations that break accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three elections before he is chosen; two sets of magistracy intervene between him and the primary assembly... By this the whole spirit of the election is changed; nor can any corrective... render him anything else than what he is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit intervening layers between primary voters and final representatives; too many intermediary bodies turn representatives into ambassadors of states rather than accountable agents of the people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disqualify experienced legislators from immediate re-service
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man who has served in an Assembly is ineligible for two years after... Just as these magistrates begin to learn their trade... they are disqualified for exercising it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rules that bar recent legislators from serving again; such purgatory intervals prevent continuity, learning, and the formation of competent governance and instead produce superficial, inexperienced governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify citizens according to real social, economic, and moral differences
rubrics_metrics.description: They had to do with men, and they were obliged to study human nature... diversities amongst men, according to their birth, their education, their professions, the periods of their lives, their residence... and according to the quality of the property itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective constitutional design recognizes different classes, habits, and functions among citizens and assigns appropriate roles/privileges to secure their interests and provide stability; flattening all distinctions into a homogeneous mass risks instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a moderating council or senate
rubrics_metrics.description: They have forgot to constitute a _senate_, or something of that nature and character... It holds a sort of middle place between the supreme power exercised by the people... and the mere executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A republican constitution should provide a deliberative or stabilizing body (senate/council) to give continuity, check rash legislation, provide a counterweight to the active assembly, and serve as a point of connection with foreign states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an executive with deliberative discretion, not a merely ceremonial or mechanical officer
rubrics_metrics.description: For this they have chosen a degraded king. This their first executive officer is to be a machine, without any sort of deliberative discretion in any one act of his function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executives should have meaningful discretionary functions and responsibility; reducing the chief executive to a mere channel to the legislature removes necessary executive judgment and weakens government functioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using confiscation and forced paper currency as the main 'cement' of the state
rubrics_metrics.description: The first is the _confiscation_, with the compulsory paper currency annexed to it... if, after a while, the confiscation should not be found sufficient to support the paper coinage... it will add infinitely to the dissociation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying on confiscation and unbacked paper money to bind political units risks short-term cohesion but long-term financial instability, loss of confidence, and political dissociation when the currency fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware creation of oligarchy via control of paper currency and land sales
rubrics_metrics.description: One thing only is certain... its effect in producing an _oligarchy_ in every one of the republics... must put the whole of what power, authority, and influence is left... into the hands of the managers and conductors of this circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies that concentrate control of currency issuance and disposal of confiscated property create powerful financial managers and speculators who can dominate politics; avoid institutional designs that centralize such fiscal power without checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid volatilizing landed property through speculation and constant transmutation into paper
rubrics_metrics.description: By this means the spirit of money-jobbing and speculation goes into the mass of land itself... it assumes an unnatural and monstrous activity... throws... all the representative of money, and perhaps a full tenth part of all the land in France, which has now acquired... the greatest possible uncertainty in its value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve stable property relations; mechanisms that convert land into speculative assets (forced sales, assignats) undermine agricultural interest, local attachments, and the social basis of rural society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not organize a polity whose economic life forces all citizens into speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Your legislators... have founded a commonwealth upon gaming, and infused this spirit into it as its vital breath... to turn its inhabitants into a nation of gamesters... speculation as extensive as life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic and monetary policy should not force ordinary people into perpetual speculation; widespread uncertainty of currency/value destroys industry, savings, and incentives to labor and investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve provincial and habitual attachments as foundations of national unity
rubrics_metrics.description: We begin our public affections in our families. We pass on to our neighborhoods, and our habitual provincial connections... Such divisions... formed by habit... were so many little images of the great country, in which the heart found something which it could fill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nation-building must respect preexisting local, provincial, and habitual ties; artificially imposing geometric or numerical divisions (square republics) that ignore these attachments will not inspire real civic affection or durable unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undue preeminence of a single city over the rest of the nation
rubrics_metrics.description: The second material of cement for their new republic is the superiority of the city of Paris... through the power of Paris... the leaders of this faction direct, or rather command, the whole legislative and the whole executive government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent concentration of political, fiscal, and social power in one urban center, which can dominate and subdue outlying regions; institutional designs should mitigate metropolitan monopolies of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide institutions that secure equality across districts by multiple securities
rubrics_metrics.description: With us the King and the Lords are several and joint securities for the equality of each district, each province, each city... the very inequality of representation... is perhaps the very thing which prevents us from thinking or acting as members for districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple, overlapping institutions (monarchy, peerage, multiple branches) can secure balance among districts and protect against arbitrary dominance; apparent inequalities in representation can play stabilizing roles if embedded in a broader constitutional structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design elections so electors can know candidates' fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: They can never know anything of the qualities of him that is to serve them, nor has he any obligation whatsoever to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral systems must provide practical means for primary electors to assess candidates (information, proximity, accountability mechanisms); otherwise elections are mockeries that fail to produce responsible representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid constituting sovereign legislative assemblies without fundamental laws or respected procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: We see a body in its constitution with every possible power and no possible external control. We see a body without fundamental laws, without established maxims, without respected rules of proceeding...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutions should limit legislative omnipotence through fundamental laws, established maxims, and respected procedural rules to prevent arbitrary, inconsistent, or destructive legislative action; absence of such constraints yields instability and potential abuse.
